title: Getting the foundations right: How South Asia can make AI work for growth
gist: World Bank South Asia VP argues the region, growing near 7 percent despite Hormuz-linked energy price pressure, should seize AI via foundations (power, skills, connectivity) and 'small AI' rather than flagship models or data centers.

insights.claim: South Asia is highly energy-dependent and relies more heavily than other regions on shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, making it vulnerable to high energy prices from the Middle East conflict.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Energy price shocks are a key downside risk for South Asian growth.

insights.claim: South Asia's growth is projected to stay near 7 percent, supported by a decade of reforms such as India's consolidated labor code and rationalized GST, Sri Lanka's tariff and revenue reforms, and Bhutan's FDI liberalization.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Reform-driven domestic demand underpins regional resilience.

insights.claim: Only 7 percent of South Asian jobs combine high AI exposure with low human complementarity, compared with 15 percent elsewhere, so more workers stand to gain than lose.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Lower displacement risk than elsewhere supports AI adoption narrative.

insights.claim: About one in four Indian firms use AI versus one in two in the United States, yet AI-skill positions already command a wage premium of nearly 30 percent.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Adoption gap implies catch-up potential and wage premiums for AI skills.

insights.claim: A one-standard-deviation rise in a U.S. firm's AI exposure after ChatGPT's launch is associated with a 27 percent larger rise in customer links with South Asian firms, so AI is deepening rather than replacing South Asia in global value chains.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: AI-adopting Western firms may expand South Asian supplier relationships.

insights.claim: South Asian firms cite digital infrastructure and tertiary education as the two biggest constraints on AI adoption, and reliable electricity, education and connectivity will spread AI more than flagship projects like frontier models or showcase data centers.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Argues against sovereign-AI flagship spending in favor of basic infrastructure.
insights.quote: reliable electricity, strong education systems, and digital connectivity will do more to spread AI's benefits broadly than any flagship project

insights.claim: The region should emphasize 'small AI': practical applications adapted to local contexts, languages and low-bandwidth devices, in sectors employing the most people.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Points to application-layer opportunities in agriculture, health and education.

insights.claim: In Telangana, AI weather forecasts save smallholder farmers up to $560 per season, and in Bangladesh AI-assisted retinal screening increased patients checked for diabetic complications by 40 percent per day.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Early evidence of productivity gains from small AI.
